Second workshop on the Code du numérique avant-projet, dating the draft as unadopted at February 2026 and naming the fibre-backbone project funding the drafting mission.

INSEED's own regulatory-texts page states the operative Loi N°026/PR/2019, INSEED's status under it and the five components of the national statistical system, with the law and its four 2019 decrees linked.

Arrêté conjoint n°070/2026 sets the composition and powers of the census's local organs and binds them to the statistics laws' response obligation and confidentiality - the statute operating, not merely existing.
Distinct instrument: Décret n°2087/PR/PM/MFBEPCI/2026 extends the RGPH-3 main enumeration to 6 August 2026 and dates the enumeration window the base does not carry.

Paragraph 13 states plainly that no freedom-of-information law has been adopted in Chad, and paragraph 19 recommends one - the dated authoritative statement of the absence, with the constitutional and press-law context.

Largest access-favourable movement in the window: the Journal Officiel digital platform launched 14 May 2026, free access to the legal record back to 1958, on a stated pillar of access to public information.

Movement in the opposite direction and a distinct event: HAMA suspends examination of online-newspaper applications until further notice, and states that digital-platform offences fall outside its competence in current law.

The enacting instrument itself: 57 articles fixing Chad's PPP legal regime, defining private financing of project phases and creating the national commission and support unit. The statute beats the World Bank profile summarising it.
Largest mobilisation event in the window, with the private share separated in the President's own words: US$4.1bn across 40 private-sector MoUs against US$16.4bn of institutional commitments.
Distinct event: Décret N°023/PR/2026 promulgates the law ratifying the UAE-Chad agreement on reciprocal promotion and protection of investments - the legal instrument behind the Abu Dhabi pledges.

ARCEP's own restitution of the 2020 market observatory and the only regulator-published internet-usage figure held: 14,2 per cent of the population using internet services in 2020, distinguished on the page itself from 53,5 per cent mobile penetration. Staged by a sibling slice at the same URL; cited here rather than duplicated.
ARCEP presented the 2024 observatory on 1 October 2025: 5,6 million internet users against 4,8 million in 2023, the first movement in the usage series inside the window.

A distinct event: ARCEP opened its fifteenth national quality-of-service audit on 16 September 2025 over complaints of slow or unavailable internet and insufficient 4G, after the fourteenth found both operators missing licence indicators.

The highest-level official statement of the affordability position: a 30 per cent cut instructed across all internet offers, reported reaching 60 to 78 per cent on some segments, with a stated target of moving cost for a SMIG earner from 17,8 per cent of salary to a band of 8 to 2. No tariff catalogue or price-ceiling instrument is published anywhere.

The Mediature de la Republique reported on 29 October 2025 that cost, quality and weak regulation are the sector's failures, and the minister of state accepted that finding and undertook to act on it.

A distinct event: at the 29 June 2026 debrief the telecommunications minister argued for restoring unlimited internet offers against Starlink's current packages, the most explicit in-window government position on offer structure.

The only primary national source naming the two state facilities and their state: the principal data centre at Klemat and the secondary at Farcha, the latter 90 per cent built. No source published anywhere gives rack count, floor area or tier.

The 19 May 2026 PMICE review: building complete and equipment installed, certification outstanding, micro data centres in public institutions awaiting configuration and interconnection. Staged by a sibling slice at the same URL; cited here rather than duplicated.
A distinct event: after the June 2026 United States mission Chad is exploring a Cybastion partnership to audit, certify and secure the centre before commissioning.

The pairing of a principal site at Klemat with a secondary site at Farcha is the whole of the public evidence that a national off-site backup architecture exists; no policy, decree or commissioning record for it was found.

The only in-window movement naming a backup facility: the 10 February 2026 joint mission inspected ADETIC's backup site, tied to service continuity, disaster recovery and resilience. Staged by a sibling slice, and filed under baseline because another indicator took it as its baseline.

The government's own energy compact of December 2024 is the standing answer to whether there is enough power for a critical load: 487 MW installed against 235 MW available, 90 per cent thermal, and 7 628 hours 41 minutes of outages on the N'Djamena network in a year.

The sharpest in-window movement against sufficiency: after the late-July 2026 Farcha 1 fire, load-shedding had run close to a month in parts of the capital as at 20 August 2026 and Tchad Elec gave no restart date.

A distinct event, and the primary source for the gap between nominal and available capacity: Noor Tchad was inaugurated at 50 MW on 28 September 2025 and the head of state stated the network can absorb only 12 MW of it.

The most recent authoritative statement of where the rural agency actually stands, from the head of state's own sectoral review: the twelve ADERM plants are meant to supply 48 MW and only 16 MW is available.

The most concrete provincial generation commitment in the window: first stone laid 17 February 2026 on three African Development Bank-financed hybrid plants at Biltine, Bol and Bongor, on a twelve-month build, with 50 schools and 50 health centres in Mayo-Kebbi Est announced alongside.

A distinct event and the largest off-grid movement: 145 000 subsidised solar kits distributed across all 23 provinces under the PAAET, with a stated reach of about 6 million people and an access target of 30 per cent by 2027.

The only document treating digital governance, public platforms, skills and institutional capacity together: platforms built in silos, no shared infrastructure or interoperability, digital skills described as very scarce, and Chad 189th of 193 on the 2022 EGDI. No published headcount of the public ICT workforce exists.

The institutional movement bearing most directly on capacity to run state systems: the Senate ratified Ordonnance n 001/PR/2026 on 13 March 2026, widening ANSICE's remit and providing for the strengthening of its technical and human means.

A distinct event: Azerbaijani ICT experts worked at ADETIC on 17 February 2026 on technical and human capacity and skills transfer, the only in-window capacity-building arrangement found with a named counterpart.

The first concrete evidence that local government holds ICT infrastructure at all: 272 964 000 FCFA of equipment handed to the 23 provincial chef-lieu communes on 19 May 2026 under the PATN. It carries in-window movement and so counts once, as the baseline.

A distinct recipient tier and purpose: on 7 January 2026 each of the 23 provincial councils received computers, solar kits, printers and a Starlink kit, to extend the SIGFiP finance system to the collectivites territoriales.

A distinct event and the only in-window evidence of a communal service actually being digitalised: mayors of the two Logone provinces trained on civil-status data collection and transmission, with TASDJIL named.

The implementing account of the move from Gesis to DHIS2, and the source that states the distinction the indicator turns on: 96,4 per cent is a figure for districts entering data directly, while the formations sanitaires filled in paper forms, with 1 798 tablets planned for offline capture. A sibling slice staged a second WHO posting of the same French report under a different filename; cited here rather than duplicated.

A distinct event: the 20 April 2026 WHO, eGov Foundation, Gates Foundation and IFRC mission to put Chad on the DIGIT platform for integrated health-campaign management, aimed at field-team tracking and data capture rather than central consolidation.

The only document that traces school data collection end to end and answers the indicator directly: at school level collection was on paper, carried up the hierarchy and keyed manually into StatEduc2 at the centre. It also identifies the founding instrument, a 2010 ministerial decree.

The largest in-window investment in the school data system: 550 000 USD of computing equipment handed over on 15 June 2026 to modernise and decentralise the SIGE, going to the planning divisions of seven provincial delegations. Staged by a sibling slice at the same URL; cited here rather than duplicated.

A distinct event and the clearest published coverage figure: SIGE decentralisation already effective in 16 provinces and to be extended to seven more under the PRET, across 12 863 primary schools as at 2025.

The dated account of what digital civil registration in Chad is: Tasdjil, offline-capable, issuing an extract with a national identification number in twenty minutes, in six hospitals in the capital and twelve provincial and district hospitals by November 2023. The largest in-window movement: the operation launched 24 July 2026 to register at least a million children across twelve provinces by December, with household enumeration by community agents equipped with smartphones. Staged by a sibling slice at the same URL; cited here rather than duplicated.

A distinct event: the Logone occidental and Logone oriental mayors trained on collection and transmission of civil-status data, with TASDJIL deployment and health-facility interoperability named, and a rise in under-one registration from 21 per cent in 2021 to 28 per cent in 2023.

The founding act: Decret n 2278 of 18 August 2023 creating CREDOP and vesting it with management of the Systeme d'information policiere du Tchad, bringing together police, gendarmerie, national and nomad guard and judicial police. Protocol of 10 March 2026 giving the finance ministry a secured channel into the biometric register for identification, verification and authentication in administrative, budgetary and financial processes

Distinct event: inauguration of the ministry centre de veille des donnees in June 2026 to consolidate DHIS2, surveillance, hospital and laboratory data

Issuing body's own description of the system holding the taxpayer register - eTAX for tele-immatriculation, tele-declaration and tele-paiement - with eTAX acquisition dated 15 May 2022 and tele-declaration launch 30 January 2023. The ministry's CGI pages are CMS stubs.

Distinct event: joint arrete of 17 August 2026 instituting the Mecanisme conjoint de coordination technique d'appui aux Chambres foncieres, putting register data in front of magistrates.

Meeting of 10 March 2026 on making the RSU interoperable with the RNBP so every entry carries a national identification number, which WFP would use as the basis of all its social assistance operations. Protocol still to be signed.

Handover of 6 February 2026 to the Cour supreme of computing, scanning, server-room and network equipment under the EU-funded PAPPE, for archive digitisation and dissemination of jurisprudence.

Distinct event: protocole d'accord with IGNFI signed in Paris on modernising geographic information systems and digitising cadastral data, with recovery of Chad's historic cartographic archives from France.

Distinct event: creation of the Direction generale de l'Intelligence Artificielle by presidential decree, 21 October 2025, the administrative pillar beside the research one. File sits under baseline/ because it is baseline for tech.ai--use-of-ai-in-government-administration; baseline wins

Chad's official statement at the first Global Dialogue on AI Governance, 7 July 2026, reaffirming the 2021 UNESCO ethics recommendation and calling for accelerated Malabo Convention implementation - a stated commitment, and the only movement found on this indicator

The Centre d'innovation technologique de N'Djamena, created by arrete n0050 of 1 September 2025 under the Presidency's secretary general and launched 30 October 2025 - the first state-founded technology hub with a founding act, ahead of the undated self-descriptions of the private hubs

Launch on 23 December 2025 of a national identification, support and financing scheme for innovative projects across all 23 provinces, run with Chad Hub Digit and ONPTA - the only in-window ecosystem movement from a publisher other than a social feed

The government's general policy declaration commits to an inclusive law-making mechanism and a citizen oversight mechanism through digital innovation; the operative statement of position.
Stakeholder consultations and a validation workshop in May 2026 put ministries, parliament, private sector, academia and civil society into the drafting of the national data governance strategy.
The only quantified national commitment on women's digital inclusion: at least 25,000 women and girls among 40,000 digital-training beneficiaries under the $92.2m Chad Digital Transformation Project.
ADETIC's own account of a free provincial digital-skills session for 100 beneficiaries explicitly open to women, January 2026.

Same document carries the only quantified disability commitment located: 2,000 people with disabilities among the project's digital-training beneficiaries. No Chadian digital-accessibility rule exists.
ANATS enrolled 400 persons with disabilities into secure QR-coded documents tied to the national identification number, July 2026 - digital identity applied to a disability caseload.
A distinct event: a three-month vocational programme for persons with disabilities including an informatique module, launched 9 May 2026. Marginal digital content, staged as such.

The regulator's own market observatory and the most recent authoritative Chadian connectivity figures; states the divide spatially (no fibre in the BET) and publishes no rural/urban table. File is shared with a sibling slice's infra.connect baseline.
A completed step: provisional acceptance of phase 1 of the state digital infrastructure project at Sarh, inaugurating the Iriba-Doba fibre line, December 2025.
A distinct event: ARCEP's fifteenth national quality-of-service audit measuring coverage province by province, 114 points and 14 road axes, October 2025.
A Chadian planning-ministry adviser names the SNDS 2021-2025 and its adoption decree, the statistics law, the FNDS and the statistical levy; the SNDS text itself is not downloadable anywhere located.
The quantified in-window movement: $105m World Bank PHASAOC financing of the national statistical system, 78 bursaries in 2024-25 and 50 further entrants, September 2025.
A distinct event: INSEED trained 90 journalists on the SSN framework and on analysing and disseminating official statistics, November 2025.

Same document is the standing statement on administrative sources: it names donnees administratives et des routines and the school, health and justice yearbooks, and the absence of statistical services in most sectoral ministries.
School administrative returns turned into validated national statistics: the education ministry's validation workshop for the 2024-2025 school statistical yearbook, October 2025.

A distinct event: the national civil-registration campaign of July 2026, smartphone-based, targeting a million children - the register from which vital statistics would come, with the size of the gap published.

The direct answer to the indicator: INSEED's national data archive is access-controlled, not open - no copying or transmission without prior written agreement, and no open licence or open-data act located.
The largest act of public-information release in the window: the digital Journal Officiel launched 14 May 2026 giving free access to laws, decrees and procurement notices back to 1958.
A distinct event: the CDIG opened its doors on 24 June 2026 presenting the Geoportail national de l'eau, the SITEAU application and new hydrogeological maps.
The standing operational use: the GIEWS Chad brief states it was built with FAO/GIEWS Earth Observation for Crop Monitoring, and publishes the cereal and food-insecurity figures that result.

The only in-window item: a national space roadmap whose short-term Chad-Eye microsatellite names agriculture, water and disaster prevention as its priority uses. An intention, and the publisher's standing is unverified.

The EIB's own words: its first targeted cooperation with the Chadian government on digitalisation and rural connectivity, three feasibility studies, framed as Team Europe. No amount attached to the digital component.
The only located instance of EU money reaching a Chadian digital deliverable inside the window: the digital Journal Officiel is EU-funded with UNDP technical support.
The only located Gulf instrument with Chad whose defined subject is digital: the October 2023 UAE cybersecurity memorandum. Secondary source; neither party published the text.
The UAE hosted the international launch of Chad Connexion 2030 on 10-11 November 2025, at which Chad states it mobilised $20.5bn; digitising the economy is a named strand with no allocation attached.
